text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- INA oil company's request for a ten percent rise in the price of gas may be met. The company is explaining its demands by saying that the kuna has slipped against the dollar by about seven percent.

- Former US negotiator in Bosnia and Herzegovina Richard Holbrooke is to return to the area of former Yugoslavia including Croatia next week as part of a US delegation looking into the implementation of the Dayton agreement.
- Privredna Banka Zagreb gets a syndicated loan worth 150 million German marks.
- The Croatian mobile phone network CRONET has 1,500 new clients each week and currently has a total of 100,000 users.
- Croatia is granted the right to appeal against the subpoena issued by the ICTY.

- The blaze on the island of Hvar in which some 3,000 hectares of pine woods, lavender fields and vineyards perished has been extinguished. None of the foreign visitors have left the island during the crisis and some even offered their help in containing the fire.
- The construction works happening across the Croatian capital are having a negative effect on the earnings of the cafes, shops and other services in Zagreb's centre.
- A Czech tourist stabs her new born baby to death and places it in her hotel room cupboard in the Istrian resort of Umag.
- The UEFA football game between rival Croatian team Croatia and Serbian team Partizan ends with no incidents reported.
- Dalmatia has seen some 1,276 fires so far in 1997.
- A gas supply line between Vinkovci and Vukovar is agreed between representatives of the INA oil company and the representatives of the Vukovar and Srijem county as part of reintegration efforts.

- The arrested retired Croatian Army general Ivan Korade is tranferred to Zagreb after spending several days at the Lora military base in Split. The Defence Ministry will inform the public of the reasons for his capture in a statement expected after Defence Minister Gojko Susak's return from the United States. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
